title: Five letters, then a story of mercy begins.
subtitle: Letters whose meaning Allah knows, a call to listen
then: This surah came in Makkah while new Muslims were being beaten, starved, and denied their wages. Later, Ja'far recited its opening to the Negus of Abyssinia when the refugees stood in his court. {idea}It begins with letters whose meaning is known to Allah alone.{/idea}
now: You open the app between a work call and the school run. Five letters you cannot translate. {idea}They slow you down.{/idea} The point is not to crack them. It is to arrive, put the phone face up, and actually hear what comes next.
old: If I cannot understand a word, there is nothing in it for me.
new: Some words are there to make me stop and pay attention before the story starts.
try: Before reading your next page of Quran, take three slow breaths and put everything else down.

title: This is a reminder of mercy to one servant.
subtitle: The surah frames Zakariyya's story as mercy

row.title: His servant
sub: an old man who earned by hand

then: Zakariyya was a great Prophet of the Children of Israel. Ibn Kathir notes he was a carpenter who ate from what he earned with his own hands. To believers who were being starved in Makkah, the surah opens with {reward}a reminder of the mercy of your Lord{/reward} to a working man.
now: You scroll past people whose lives look blessed: big houses, perfect trips. Your life is a shift, a bus, a fridge to fill. {reward}The mercy story starts with a carpenter.{/reward} It is told so you remember it can reach you too.
old: Allah's special mercy is for people more important than me.
new: Mercy is told through an ordinary servant so I know it is meant for servants like me.
try: Write down one mercy in your life this week that nobody else would notice.

title: He called his Lord in a quiet, private voice.
subtitle: The hidden prayer that Allah loves
then: Zakariyya made his supplication secretly. Ibn Kathir says this is more beloved to Allah, and quotes Qatadah: {idea}Allah knows the pious heart and hears the hidden voice.{/idea}
now: Late at night, the house asleep, you whisper something you would never post or tell your friends. It feels too small, too private to matter. {idea}That whisper is exactly the kind of call this verse describes.{/idea}
old: A prayer only matters if it is big, formal, or seen.
new: The quiet ask that no one else hears is the one Allah loves most.
try: Tonight, ask Allah for one thing in a whisper, in your own words.

title: Weak bones, white hair, and a lifetime of answered prayers.
subtitle: He names his weakness and Allah's record
then: Zakariyya describes his old age: his bones have weakened and grey has burned into his black hair. Then he says he has never been unblessed in calling on Allah. {reward}Ibn Kathir explains: You have always answered me, and never refused me.{/reward}
now: The doctor's letter. The mirror in the morning. The feeling that your best years for asking are behind you. {idea}Zakariyya leads with his weakness and then remembers every time Allah came through.{/idea} Your history with Allah is your reason to keep asking.
old: My weakness is a reason not to bother asking anymore.
new: My weakness is something I can tell Allah, next to all the times He already answered me.
try: Recall three prayers of yours that were answered, then make one new one.

title: Worried about who would carry the faith after him.
subtitle: A barren wife, a worrying future, a bold request
then: Zakariyya feared his relatives after him would be a corrupt generation. Ibn Kathir stresses he was {idea}not worried about wealth{/idea}: he was a carpenter, and Prophets do not leave wealth as inheritance. He wanted someone to keep guiding people.
now: You look at the younger ones in your family and wonder who will keep the prayers alive after you. {trap}From where you stand, it looks unlikely.{/trap} Zakariyya's wife was barren and he still asked, from Allah Himself.
old: When something looks impossible, it is not worth asking for.
new: When I care about faith continuing, I can ask Allah for it directly, even against the odds.
try: Make a short dua today for one young person in your family by name.

title: An heir of knowledge, and one Allah is pleased with.
subtitle: What Zakariyya actually wanted passed on

key.label: What he asked for in the child

then: Ibn Kathir explains the inheritance meant prophethood and knowledge, like Sulayman inheriting from Dawud. Mujahid said his inheritance was knowledge. {reward}Make him pleasing{/reward} means: pleasing to Allah, and beloved to people in religion and character.
now: Parents' evening. The talk about grades, universities, salaries. You want the best for your child, and that list is usually about the CV. {idea}Zakariyya's list was about character and being loved by Allah.{/idea}
old: What I most want to leave my children is money and a good start.
new: The best thing to pass on is faith and good character that Allah is pleased with.
try: Tell a child in your life one thing you admire about their character, not their results.

title: The answer came with a name no one had before.
subtitle: Good news of Yahya
then: The verse skips straight to the result: the prayer was answered. In Surah Al Imran the angels called Zakariyya while he stood praying in the Mihrab. {reward}Allah even named the boy, Yahya, a name no one had carried before.{/reward}
now: You have asked for something for years. A job, a child, a healing. You start to think it got lost somewhere. {reward}This verse shows how fully an answer can arrive, down to the name.{/reward}
old: My long-standing prayer has probably been forgotten.
new: Allah hears it in full detail, and His answer can be more personal than I imagined.
try: Bring back one old dua you stopped making, and make it again today.

title: Overjoyed, he asked: how can this even happen?
subtitle: Amazement at an answered prayer
then: Ibn Kathir says Zakariyya was {reward}extremely overjoyed{/reward} and asked how the child would come. His wife was old and had never had children, and he himself was very old and weak.
now: The acceptance email arrives. The scan shows a heartbeat. You read it four times and say: how? {idea}Asking how, in wonder, is not a lack of faith.{/idea} It is what joy sounds like when the odds were against you.
old: Being amazed by an answer means I did not really believe.
new: Wonder at what Allah does is a natural, honest response to His gifts.
try: Tell someone today about one thing Allah gave you that you did not expect.

title: Easy for Me: I made you from nothing.
subtitle: The bigger miracle answers the smaller one
then: The angel answered that Allah says it is easy for Him. Then {idea}he pointed to something more amazing{/idea}: Allah created Zakariyya himself when he was nothing. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse about a time when man was not a thing worth mentioning.
now: You are sitting in the waiting room thinking the problem is too big. Look at your own hands. {idea}A while ago, you did not exist at all.{/idea} The One who did that is not stretched by what you are asking.
old: My problem is too big to be fixed.
new: I am proof that Allah makes things from nothing. My problem is small next to that.
try: When a worry feels huge today, remind yourself: He made me from nothing.

title: He asked for a sign so his heart could rest.
subtitle: Three nights of silence while perfectly healthy
then: Ibn Kathir says Zakariyya wanted proof so {idea}his soul would be at rest{/idea} with the promise, as Ibrahim asked to see how Allah gives life. His sign: he could not speak to people for three nights, though healthy, and only gestured.
now: You believe, but your heart still races at 3am. You want something to hold onto. {idea}Asking Allah for reassurance is not the same as not trusting Him.{/idea} Even Prophets asked for calm hearts.
old: If I needed reassurance, my faith must be weak.
new: Wanting my heart to settle is human, and I can ask Allah for that too.
try: Ask Allah tonight, simply: make my heart calm about this.

title: Unable to speak, he signaled: glorify Allah morning and evening.
subtitle: Silence turned into gratitude

picture.label: What he did with the silence

then: Zakariyya came out of the Mihrab, the place where he got the good news. He could not speak, so he made a quick gesture to his people: glorify Allah morning and evening. Ibn Kathir says these days were for {reward}increasing in deeds and gratitude{/reward}.
now: Good news lands and your thumb is already on the group chat. Before the photos, the calls, the congratulations, {reward}there is a quieter first response: thanking the One who gave it.{/reward}
old: When something good happens, the first thing to do is share it.
new: The first thing to do with a gift is turn back to the Giver in thanks.
try: Next time good news comes, say alhamdulillah before you tell anyone.

title: Take the Book with strength, even as a boy.
subtitle: Yahya, wise while still a child
then: The promised boy was born. Allah taught him the Tawrah while he was young. {idea}Hold it with strength{/idea} means, as Ibn Kathir says, learn it well, with zeal and studious effort. He was given understanding and a drive for good while still a child.
now: You are fifteen, or forty, and your Quran app streak keeps breaking. You think real commitment will come later, when life calms down. {idea}Strength here means effort now, at whatever age you are.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about my faith when I am older or less busy.
new: Holding the Book firmly is something I can start now, at my age.
try: Pick one verse and learn its meaning properly today, with full attention.

title: Tenderness and purity, gifts straight from Allah.
subtitle: Yahya's soft heart and clean conduct
then: Ibn Abbas said the affection here means mercy from Allah. Ibn Kathir explains Allah gave Yahya {reward}wisdom, compassion and purity together{/reward}: a gentle, tender man, clean of sin, who was mindful of Allah.
now: The person who knows the most in the family WhatsApp group is often the harshest one in it. {trap}Right facts, cold tone.{/trap} Yahya's knowledge came wrapped in tenderness, and that combination was itself a gift.
old: Being right is more important than being gentle.
new: Real wisdom comes with a soft heart toward people.
try: In your next disagreement, say your point once, gently, and then let it rest.

title: Kind to his parents, never arrogant or rebellious.
subtitle: Devotion to Allah shown in how he treated parents
then: After describing Yahya's devotion to Allah, the verse turns to his {reward}good treatment of his parents{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says he never disobeyed them in speech, actions, or their instructions, and he was {trap}never arrogant or rebellious{/trap}.
now: Your mum calls for the third time while you are busy. Your dad repeats the same story at dinner. {idea}This is where Yahya's piety would have shown up: in the tone of your reply.{/idea}
old: My worship is between me and Allah; how I talk to my parents is separate.
new: Being good to my parents is part of the same devotion.
try: Call or message a parent today just to ask how they are, with no request.

title: Peace on him at birth, at death, and when raised.
subtitle: Safety in the three loneliest moments
then: After listing Yahya's qualities, Allah gives his reward: peace on three days. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said these are {trap}the loneliest moments a person ever feels{/trap}: birth, death, and the resurrection. Allah honored Yahya with {reward}safety in all three{/reward}.
now: The hospital corridor where a baby is born, the one where someone is dying. You have stood in both and felt how alone a person is in them. {reward}Yahya's character earned him peace in exactly those moments.{/reward}
old: The hardest moments of life are ones I just have to face alone.
new: How I live now shapes whether peace meets me in those moments.
try: Ask Allah today for peace on the day you die and the day you are raised.

title: Maryam stepped away from her family to be alone.
subtitle: A devoted worshipper withdraws to the east
then: After Zakariyya's story, the surah turns to Maryam. Ibn Kathir says she came from a good family, was {reward}dedicated by her mother to the service of Allah{/reward}, and was known for her worship. She withdrew from her family to a place on the eastern side of the Sacred House.
now: The house is loud. The phone is louder. You go and sit in the car in the driveway for ten quiet minutes. {idea}Stepping away to be alone with Allah is where this story's miracle begins.{/idea}
old: Taking time alone is a waste when there is so much to do.
new: Withdrawing to be with Allah can be the most important part of my day.
try: Find ten minutes today in a quiet place with no phone, and spend them in dhikr.

title: Behind her screen, an angel appeared as a man.
subtitle: Jibril is sent to Maryam

key.label: What she expected vs what came

then: Maryam hid herself from her people behind a screen. Then Allah sent His Ruh, which the early scholars say means {idea}Jibril{/idea}. He came to her in the form of a perfect, complete man.
now: You sit down for an ordinary moment of worship. Nothing seems special about the evening. {reward}Some of the biggest turns in a life arrive in exactly those quiet, private hours.{/reward}
old: Nothing big happens in my small private moments with Allah.
new: The hidden hour of worship is where Allah's plans often begin.
try: Keep one small private act of worship today that only Allah sees.

title: Afraid, she sought refuge in the Most Merciful.
subtitle: Her first defense was reminding him of Allah
then: Alone, Maryam saw a man and feared he meant to harm her. {idea}The first thing she did was seek refuge in Allah and try to make him fear Allah.{/idea} Abu Wa'il said she knew a God-fearing person would hold back from evil.
now: A message that feels threatening. A man in the car park who will not leave you alone. {trap}Your heart is pounding.{/trap} Maryam's first move was to say Allah's name, and to call on the other person's conscience.
old: When I am scared, there is no time to think of Allah.
new: Turning to Allah first, out loud, is itself a defense.
try: Memorize a short line of seeking refuge, like a'udhu billah, for moments of fear.

title: I am only your Lord's messenger, bringing a pure son.
subtitle: The angel calms her fear
then: Ibn Kathir says the angel answered {idea}to remove the fear she felt{/idea}: I am not what you think, I am your Lord's messenger. He had come with the gift of a pure, righteous son.
now: The unknown number keeps calling, and you assume the worst. A letter with an official stamp sits unopened on the table. {reward}Sometimes the thing you are dreading is carrying good news.{/reward}
old: Anything unexpected is probably bad.
new: What scares me at first may turn out to be a gift sent by Allah.
try: Open one thing you have been avoiding out of fear today, with bismillah.

title: How, when no man has touched me?
subtitle: Maryam's honest question about her own purity
then: Maryam was amazed. Ibn Kathir explains her words as: {idea}in what way would a son come to me{/idea}, when I have no husband and have done nothing wrong? Like Zakariyya before her, she asked how.
now: Life hands you something that does not fit any category you know. You are allowed to say: I do not understand how this works. {idea}Maryam's question is honest, and it is answered.{/idea}
old: Asking how something can be means I am resisting Allah.
new: I can bring my honest questions to Allah and still accept His decree.
try: Write down one question you have about your situation, and ask Allah to show you.

title: Easy for Allah: a sign for people and a mercy.
subtitle: Why Isa would be born without a father

picture.label: Four ways to create a human

then: The angel said it is easy for Allah. Ibn Kathir explains Isa would be {idea}a sign of Allah's power{/idea}: Adam had no parents, Hawwa came from a male, the rest of us from both, and Isa from a mother alone. It was a matter already decreed.
now: Your life is taking a shape you did not plan, and people around you will have opinions. {reward}What looks strange from outside may be exactly what Allah intended, and a mercy.{/reward}
old: If my story looks unusual, something must have gone wrong.
new: Allah can make an unusual path into a sign and a mercy.
try: Say to yourself today about one unplanned turn: this was already decreed, and Allah is merciful.

title: She accepted the decree and carried it far away.
subtitle: Pregnancy, rumors, and a remote place
then: Ibn Kathir says Maryam {reward}accepted the decree of Allah{/reward} and conceived. Ibn Ishaq describes her pregnancy sickness and how {trap}word spread among the people{/trap}. She hid herself away and withdrew to a far place.
now: You said yes to something you believe is from Allah: a hard marriage, a sick parent to care for, a move. And then the talk started at family gatherings. {idea}Accepting the decree did not make Maryam's road easy.{/idea}
old: If this is really from Allah, it should feel easy.
new: Accepting Allah's decree can still mean a hard, lonely road.
try: Send a kind message to someone carrying something hard that others gossip about.

title: In labor pain she said: I wish I had died before this.
subtitle: Even the best can reach the edge
then: The pains of labor drove her to the trunk of a date palm. Ibn Kathir says she knew {trap}people would not help her or believe her story{/trap}, after being known as a devout worshipper. She wished she had been nothing, forgotten.
now: Two in the morning, in pain, sure that everyone will judge you, you say: I cannot do this anymore. {idea}Allah put Maryam's same words in the Quran.{/idea} Hitting that wall does not mean you are far from Him.
old: If I ever feel like giving up, I have failed as a believer.
new: Even Maryam reached the edge, and Allah's help came right after.
try: If you are at the edge today, tell Allah exactly how you feel, then tell one trusted person.

title: Do not grieve: a stream is already beneath you.
subtitle: Comfort arrives at her lowest point
then: A voice called from below her. Some scholars say it was Jibril, others say Isa. It said {idea}do not grieve{/idea}: your Lord has placed a stream beneath you. Al-Bara and Ibn Abbas said the word means a small river for her to drink.
now: You feel completely alone. Then the neighbor knocks with food, or a friend calls at the right minute. {reward}The help was already near; you just could not see it from the floor.{/reward}
old: When I hit bottom, nobody and nothing is there for me.
new: Allah's provision can already be beneath me when I feel most alone.
try: Look around today and name one help you already have that you overlooked.

title: Shake the trunk, and fresh dates will fall.
subtitle: Allah provides, and she still has a part to play
then: She was told to grab the trunk of the date palm and shake it toward herself. {reward}Allah blessed her with food and drink.{/reward} Amr bin Maymun said nothing is better for a woman after childbirth than dates.
now: You are worn out after a long week and the job search feels pointless. One more application. One phone call. {idea}A tired woman could not truly shake a palm tree, yet she was told to try.{/idea}
old: My little effort is too small to make any difference.
new: Allah asks for my small effort and then sends the provision Himself.
try: Do one small step today on something you have been waiting on.

title: Eat, drink, be at peace, and let silence speak.
subtitle: She does not have to defend herself
then: She was told to eat, drink and be glad. If anyone came, she should signal that she had vowed a fast of silence to the Most Merciful. Ibn Kathir says {idea}her affair would be taken care of and her proof established{/idea}.
now: The family group chat is full of questions about you. You draft a long reply, delete it, draft again. {idea}Sometimes the strongest answer is to eat, rest, and let Allah show the truth.{/idea}
old: If I do not defend myself to everyone, they will believe the worst.
new: I can stay calm and quiet and trust Allah to clear my name.
try: Skip one argument today where you feel you must justify yourself.

title: She carried her baby straight into the accusations.
subtitle: Maryam faces her people
then: Maryam accepted Allah's command and {idea}readily received His decree{/idea}. She took her child and brought him to her people. When they saw her, {trap}they made a big deal of it and protested sternly{/trap}: you have brought something terrible.
now: You have to walk into the family dinner where everyone has already heard a version of your story. Your stomach drops in the car park. {idea}Maryam walked in holding the very thing they would accuse her over, trusting Allah to speak for her.{/idea}
old: I cannot face people until I have every answer ready.
new: I can face people with trust in Allah, even before I can explain myself.
try: Face one conversation you have been avoiding, and say a short dua before you go in.

title: Sister of Harun, your family was never like this.
subtitle: They used her good family against her
then: They called her {idea}sister of Harun{/idea}, meaning one who resembled him in worship, or a descendant of his line. Then they said: you come from a pure family known for righteousness. {trap}How could you do such a thing?{/trap}
now: Someone says: your parents are such good people, how could you? It hurts more because it uses love as a weapon. {trap}They are judging the surface.{/trap} The full truth is not always visible to the people who talk the most.
old: If my respected family sees it badly, it must be bad.
new: People, even good ones, can judge wrongly when the truth is hidden from them.
try: Next time you hear a story about someone, hold your judgment until you know more.

title: She just pointed at the baby.
subtitle: Silence, then she hands the answer over
then: Maryam was fasting from speech, so she {idea}referred all speech to the child{/idea}. They thought she was playing with them. As-Suddi said they became angrier, saying her mocking them was worse than the accusation itself.
now: You did what you believed was right and now it looks ridiculous to everyone in the room. They laugh. {idea}Maryam's gesture looked foolish for a few seconds, right before Allah answered for her.{/idea}
old: If doing the right thing makes me look foolish, I should stop.
new: Trusting Allah can look foolish for a moment before it is proved right.
try: Do one right thing today even if someone might laugh at it.

title: The baby spoke: I am the servant of Allah.
subtitle: Isa's first words, from the cradle

key.label: His first words did two things

then: Ibn Kathir says Isa's first words declared {idea}the honor of his Lord and that Allah has no child{/idea}, and that he himself worshipped Allah. Saying Allah made him a Prophet was {reward}a declaration of his mother's innocence{/reward}.
now: You introduce yourself all the time: job title, city, whose son or daughter. {idea}Isa's very first words about himself were: servant of Allah.{/idea} Everything else came after that.
old: Who I am is my job, my family, my achievements.
new: The first and truest thing about me is that I am Allah's servant.
try: Before you start work today, remind yourself: I am Allah's servant first.

title: Blessed wherever I am, with prayer and charity for life.
subtitle: A blessing that travels with you
then: Mujahid explained blessed wherever I am as {reward}a teacher of goodness, a person of great benefit{/reward}. Wuhayb bin Al-Ward said his blessing was commanding good and forbidding evil wherever he was. Prayer and zakah were enjoined on him {idea}for his whole life{/idea}.
now: The new office. The hospital ward. The football club where you coach on Saturdays. {reward}Being blessed is not about things going well for you; it is about people being better off because you were there.{/reward}
old: I will be blessed when life gets easier for me.
new: I am blessed when I bring good to whatever place I am in.
try: In one place you go today, leave one small good behind: help, a kind word, a tidy space.

title: Dutiful to my mother, never a wretched tyrant.
subtitle: Worship of Allah paired with kindness to a mother
then: Isa said Allah commanded him to treat his mother well. Ibn Kathir notes this comes after obedience to Allah because {idea}Allah often joins worship of Him with kindness to parents{/idea}, as in Surah Al-Isra. Maryam had just endured everything for this child.
now: Your mother sacrificed in ways you probably never saw: the nights, the worries, what people said. {reward}Isa's words for his mother came in the same breath as his worship.{/reward} Your tone with her is part of your religion.
old: Being religious is about prayer; family is a separate thing.
new: Kindness to my mother is joined to my worship of Allah.
try: Do one thing for your mother today without being asked, or make dua for her by name.

title: Peace on me at birth, at death, and when raised.
subtitle: Isa echoes the peace given to Yahya

key.label: What was true of his birth

then: The baby finished his words: peace on the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised. The people had just called his birth {trap}a terrible thing{/trap}. {reward}Allah called it a day of peace.{/reward}
now: Someone has written a story about you: the gossip at work, the label from school. It sticks. {reward}What people call your story and what Allah calls it can be completely different.{/reward}
old: What people say about my life is the final word on it.
new: Allah's word on my life outweighs every rumor about it.
try: Let go of one label someone gave you, and ask Allah for peace on your three days.

title: That is Isa, son of Maryam: the word of truth.
subtitle: The story told plainly, after all the dispute
then: Allah tells Muhammad ﷺ: this is the story of Isa. Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}a statement of truth{/idea}, about which the people of truth and falsehood disagree. In Surah Al Imran: the truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
now: You read ten threads about something important and each one says something different. Your head spins. {idea}This verse plants a flag: here is the truth from Allah, said simply.{/idea}
old: With so many opinions, I can never know what is true.
new: Allah has told the truth plainly; I can hold onto it amid the noise.
try: Close one argument thread you are scrolling today and read a page of Quran instead.

title: No son for Allah: He says Be, and it is.
subtitle: Glory to Him, above what is said about Him
then: After showing Isa as servant and Prophet, Allah {idea}glorifies Himself{/idea}: it does not befit Him to take a son. Whenever He wants something, He commands it and it happens. Ibn Kathir links this to Surah Al Imran: Isa is like Adam, created from dust with the word Be.
now: You picture Allah through human limits: tired, needing help, needing heirs. {idea}He needs nothing.{/idea} The plans you are worried about are, for Him, one word.
old: Allah works the way people work, with limits and needs.
new: Allah needs no one; He says Be, and it is.
try: Say subhanallah slowly ten times today, thinking about what it means.

title: Allah is my Lord and your Lord: worship Him.
subtitle: Isa's message, the straight path
then: Among what Isa said from the cradle: {idea}Allah is my Lord and your Lord{/idea}, so worship Him alone. Ibn Kathir explains: what I bring from Allah is the straight path. Whoever follows it is guided.
now: Prayer time, and you are next to a stranger at the airport prayer room. Different language, different background. {idea}Same Lord.{/idea} The straight path is simple enough to say in one sentence.
old: Faith is complicated and only experts can find the right path.
new: The straight path is clear: one Lord for all of us, worship Him.
try: Pray your next prayer remembering: He is my Lord and the Lord of everyone praying with me.

title: Then factions split, even after it was made clear.
subtitle: Disagreement after clarity, and a great Day ahead
then: Ibn Kathir says opinions about Isa differed {trap}even after his affair was explained{/trap}. The warning of the great Day is for those who lie about Allah. Yet Allah {idea}gives respite{/idea}; the Prophet ﷺ said no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah, who still provides for them.
now: You already know the right thing in some area of your life, but you keep arguing yourself out of it. {idea}Allah's patience with you is real.{/idea} It is time given, not permission.
old: Since nothing has happened to me, it must not matter.
new: Allah's delay is patience and a chance to return, not a sign that He does not see.
try: Pick one thing you know is right but keep putting off, and start it today.

title: On that Day everyone will see and hear clearly.
subtitle: Clear sight that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Resurrection the wrongdoers will have the clearest hearing and sight, saying: our Lord, now we have seen and heard. {trap}But it will not help them then.{/trap} {reward}If they had used these senses before, it would have benefited them.{/reward}
now: The day after the argument, you see clearly what you should have said. After the diagnosis, you see the warnings. {reward}This verse asks you to use your eyes and ears now, while seeing still changes something.{/reward}
old: I will think about the big questions later.
new: Clarity is only useful while I still have time to act on it.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: what am I choosing not to see?

title: Warn of the Day of Regret, while people are heedless.
subtitle: When the matter is decided for good
then: The Prophet ﷺ described death brought between Paradise and the Fire and slaughtered, with eternity declared for both. Then he recited this verse and said: {trap}the people of this life are in heedlessness of this life.{/trap} Ibn Mas'ud said every soul will see a home in each.
now: Notifications, deadlines, the next episode starting in five seconds. {trap}Heedlessness rarely feels like rejecting anything.{/trap} It feels like being busy. {reward}The door is still open today.{/reward}
old: I am not rejecting anything; I am just busy.
new: Busy distraction is the heedlessness this verse warns about, and today I can still choose.
try: Turn off autoplay or one notification today and use those minutes to remember Allah.

title: Allah inherits the earth and all on it.
subtitle: Everything returns to its true Owner
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is the Creator, Owner and Controller of all. {idea}All creation will pass and only He remains.{/idea} He judges, and no soul will be wronged even an atom's weight. Umar bin Abdul-Aziz quoted this verse in a letter to his governor.
now: The house deeds with your name on them. The inheritance argument in the family. {idea}Every name on every title deed is temporary.{/idea} The One who inherits it all is also the One who judges fairly.
old: What I have built and own is mine to keep.
new: Everything I hold returns to Allah; I am only looking after it for a while.
try: Give away or lend one thing you own today, remembering it was never fully yours.

title: Ibrahim, a man of truth and a Prophet.
subtitle: The ancestor Quraysh claimed, retold to them
then: Allah tells Muhammad ﷺ to recite this to his idol-worshipping people. Ibn Kathir notes {trap}they were Ibrahim's descendants and claimed to follow his religion{/trap}. So remind them: {idea}he was a truthful Prophet{/idea}, and listen to what he told his own father.
now: You come from a religious family. Your grandfather prayed every prayer in the mosque. {trap}It is easy to feel that some of that counts for you.{/trap} The verse asks: are you living what your ancestors are praised for?
old: My family's faith covers me.
new: Being linked to good people means nothing unless I follow what they did.
try: Name one habit of a righteous elder in your family and practice it today.

title: O my father, why worship what cannot hear or see?
subtitle: A son's gentle first question
then: Ibrahim spoke to his own father about the idols. He opened with {idea}O my father{/idea} and a question: why worship things that hear nothing, see nothing, and {trap}cannot benefit or protect you{/trap}?
now: Your dad trusts something that is hurting him: a scheme, a habit, a belief. You want to shout. {idea}Ibrahim began with a tender title and an honest question.{/idea}
old: When someone I love is wrong, I need to hit hard so they get it.
new: The truth lands better when it starts with love and a real question.
try: In one hard talk with family this week, open with a kind word before your point.

title: I have knowledge you do not; follow me to a straight path.
subtitle: A son offering to guide his father
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim's words: even though I am your son and {trap}you see me as lesser{/trap}, I have received knowledge from Allah that has not reached you. {reward}Follow me and I will guide you to a straight path{/reward} that saves you.
now: Your teenager shows you something true from a class or a lecture, and your first instinct is: what do you know? {idea}Truth can come through someone younger than you.{/idea}
old: I am older, so I do not need to learn from them.
new: Allah can send guidance to me through anyone, even my own child.
try: Ask someone younger than you to teach you one thing today, and listen fully.

title: Do not worship Shaytan, the rebel against the Most Merciful.
subtitle: Behind the idols stands an obedience to Shaytan
then: Ibn Kathir explains: do not obey Shaytan by worshipping idols, since {trap}he invites to it and is pleased with it{/trap}. Shaytan was obstinate and {trap}too arrogant to obey his Lord{/trap}, so Allah expelled him. Follow him and you become like him.
now: Nobody thinks they serve Shaytan. You just keep doing the thing you promised to stop, at midnight, on your phone. {idea}Whose voice are you really obeying?{/idea}
old: I do not worship anything except Allah, so this does not apply to me.
new: Whatever voice I keep obeying against Allah is the one I am serving.
try: Notice one moment today when you are pulled to something wrong, and say a'udhu billah.

title: I fear for you, my father.
subtitle: A warning spoken out of love
then: Ibrahim said he feared a punishment would reach his father. Ibn Kathir explains that then {trap}no one would help him except Shaytan, who has no power over the outcome{/trap}. Even here he names Allah as {idea}the Most Merciful{/idea}.
now: You worry about a parent who has drifted far from prayer. You can lecture, or you can say, gently: I am scared for you, because I love you. {idea}Ibrahim's warning sounds like the second one.{/idea}
old: Warning someone means being harsh with them.
new: A real warning comes from fear for the person, said with love.
try: Make sincere dua today for one family member you worry about.

title: His father threatened to stone him and drove him away.
subtitle: Gentle words answered with threats
then: Ibrahim's father replied: do you turn away from my gods? Ibn Kathir says he meant {trap}stop speaking against them or I will punish and curse you{/trap}. He told his son to leave, some said forever, others said to go safely before harm came to him.
now: You chose your words with care, and the reply in the group chat was cruel. {trap}Being gentle did not make them listen.{/trap} Ibrahim did everything right, and still heard this from his own father.
old: If they reject me, I must have said it wrong.
new: I can say it well and still be rejected; that is not my failure.
try: Forgive yourself for one conversation that went badly even though you meant well.

title: Peace be on you: I will ask my Lord to forgive you.
subtitle: Ibrahim answers a threat with peace
then: Ibrahim said peace be on you. Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}you will receive no insult or harm from me{/reward}, out of respect for fatherhood. It matches how the believers answer the foolish with peace. He said his Lord had always been {idea}kind to him{/idea}.
now: Your father says something deeply hurtful at the dinner table. Every part of you wants to fire back. {reward}Ibrahim's reply was: peace on you, I will pray for you.{/reward}
old: If someone attacks me, I have the right to hit back just as hard.
new: I can answer harshness with peace and a prayer, and keep my dignity.
try: The next time someone is harsh with you today, reply with one calm, peaceful sentence.

title: I will leave you and call on my Lord alone.
subtitle: Walking away without losing hope
then: Ibrahim said he would separate from them and worship his Lord alone. He hoped he would not be unblessed in calling on Him. Ibn Kathir says this hope means something {reward}certain to happen{/reward}, not a wish for the impossible.
now: You have to leave a place that keeps pulling you away from Allah: a friendship circle, a workplace, a house. {idea}Leaving is not the end of your story.{/idea} Ibrahim walked out still talking to his Lord, sure of being heard.
old: If I walk away from people, I am left with nothing.
new: When I leave for Allah's sake, I am walking toward Him, not into emptiness.
try: If something keeps pulling you from Allah, take one small step back from it today.

title: He left them for Allah, and Allah gave him Ishaq and Ya'qub.
subtitle: What he lost was replaced with something better
then: Ibn Kathir says when Ibrahim withdrew from his father and people for Allah's sake, {reward}Allah gave him in exchange people better than them{/reward}: his son Ishaq and grandson Ya'qub, each a Prophet, to give him joy in his life.
now: You stepped away from the old friends, the old crowd. The weekends are quieter and you wonder if you just lost everything. {reward}Allah does not leave a gap where someone left for Him.{/reward}
old: What I give up for Allah is simply gone.
new: Allah replaces what I leave for Him with something better.
try: Thank Allah today for one good person who came into your life after a hard goodbye.

title: Mercy, and a name honored on every tongue.
subtitle: A lasting good reputation as a gift
then: Ibn Abbas said this means {reward}good praise{/reward}. Ibn Jarir explained it is called lofty because all religions mention them with praise. The man his father drove away became honored by people for ages.
now: You did the right thing at work and your name got dragged in the office for it. {reward}The reputation that lasts is the one Allah gives.{/reward} The office will forget; Allah does not.
old: My reputation depends on what people around me say now.
new: The honor that lasts is the one Allah puts on people's tongues.
try: Do one good thing today that no one will credit you for.

title: Musa: chosen, sincere, a Messenger and a Prophet.
subtitle: Sincerity means not wanting people's praise
then: The disciples asked Isa who is sincere to Allah. He said: {idea}one who does a deed solely for Allah and does not like people to praise him{/idea}. Musa was one of the five Messengers of strong will: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad ﷺ.
now: You helped someone and then checked whether anyone noticed. You posted the charity receipt. {idea}Sincerity is doing the good thing and not needing the likes.{/idea}
old: A good deed counts more if people see it.
new: A deed is purest when I do it for Allah and do not want the praise.
try: Do one good deed today and tell no one about it.

title: Called from the mountain and drawn near to talk.
subtitle: Musa went looking for fire and found his Lord

key.label: What he went for vs found

row.title: his Lord's call
sub: the turning point of his life

then: Musa saw a glow in the distance and went to get some burning wood. He found it on the right side of the mountain. {reward}There Allah called him, drew him near, and spoke with him.{/reward}
now: You went to the mosque for the free dinner, or opened the app just to check a word. {reward}Ordinary errands can turn into the moment Allah calls you closer.{/reward}
old: Only big spiritual journeys bring me close to Allah.
new: Allah can call me near in the middle of an ordinary errand.
try: Treat one ordinary trip today as a chance to remember Allah on the way.

title: Out of mercy, Allah gave Musa his brother as a Prophet.
subtitle: The answered plea for a brother
then: Allah answered Musa's plea for his brother and made Harun a Prophet. Musa had said Harun was more eloquent and could help confirm him. {reward}Some of the early scholars said no one ever pleaded for another more than Musa did for his brother.{/reward}
now: Your sibling is struggling: a job, a marriage, faith. You usually pray for yourself first and fastest. {reward}Musa used one of his biggest requests for his brother.{/reward}
old: My duas are mostly for my own needs.
new: Asking Allah for good for my sibling is one of the best duas I can make.
try: Make one sincere dua for a brother or sister by name today, and tell them you did.

title: Isma'il kept his promises.
subtitle: True to his word, a Messenger and a Prophet
then: Ibn Jurayj said Isma'il {reward}never made a promise to his Lord without fulfilling it{/reward}. Some link it to his words to his father: you will find me patient. The Prophet ﷺ said {trap}breaking a promise is a sign of the hypocrite{/trap}, and he himself kept every promise.
now: I will call you back. I will pay you Friday. I will come to your event. {trap}Small promises slip easily.{/trap} {reward}Isma'il is praised by Allah for simply keeping his word.{/reward}
old: Small promises do not really matter.
new: Keeping my word, even in small things, is something Allah praises.
try: Keep one small promise today that you have been putting off.

title: He reminded his family to pray and give, and Allah was pleased.
subtitle: Faith carried into the home
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a beautiful praise: Isma'il {idea}persisted in obeying his Lord and urged his family to do the same{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ prayed for mercy on a spouse who rises at night to pray and wakes the other. {reward}His Lord was pleased with him.{/reward}
now: Fajr alarm. You get up, and the rest of the house sleeps on. {idea}A soft knock on a door, a glass of water, a gentle reminder.{/idea} Faith in a home grows when someone keeps inviting, patiently.
old: Everyone in my family is responsible for their own prayers; it is not my business.
new: Gently helping my family toward prayer is part of my own faith.
try: Invite one family member to pray one prayer together today.

title: Idris, a man of truth and a Prophet.
subtitle: Truthfulness named as his defining trait
then: After Ibrahim, Musa and Isma'il, the surah mentions Idris. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah complimented him for being a truthful Prophet{/reward}. The Quran gives few details of his life, but it names this one quality.
now: Someday people will sum you up in one line at your funeral. Funny, hard-working, generous. {reward}Allah summed up Idris in one word: truthful.{/reward} What would your one word be?
old: Honesty is nice, but it is not what defines a person.
new: Being truthful can be the one thing my whole life is remembered for.
try: Go through today without a single small lie, even a polite one.

title: Allah raised Idris to a high station.
subtitle: Raised up because of who he was
then: The Prophet ﷺ passed by Idris in the fourth heaven on the night of the Isra. Mujahid said the high station is the fourth heaven; Al-Hasan said it means Paradise. {reward}Either way, it is Allah who raised him.{/reward}
now: The promotion went to someone louder. Your quiet honesty never trends. {reward}Allah raises people for reasons the world does not measure.{/reward}
old: If people do not lift me up, I will never rise.
new: Allah raises the truthful, whether or not people notice.
try: Do your work honestly today and leave the recognition to Allah.

title: When they heard His verses, they fell down weeping.
subtitle: The Prophets' response to Allah's words
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to all the Prophets. When they heard Allah's words and His signs, {idea}they prostrated in humility, praise and thanks for the favors they were given{/idea}, and they wept. Ibn Abbas cited: they are those Allah guided, so follow their guidance.
now: The recitation plays in the car while you are thinking about traffic and dinner. {idea}For the best people who ever lived, those same words brought them to the floor in tears.{/idea}
old: Listening to Quran is something to have on in the background.
new: Allah's words deserve to be heard with a heart that can be moved.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else going on, and let it reach you.

title: Then came generations who neglected prayer and chased desires.
subtitle: What happens after the good ones are gone
then: After the Prophets came later generations. Ibn Mas'ud, Masruq and Umar bin Abdul-Aziz all said {trap}their loss was praying outside the proper times{/trap}, not total abandonment. Prayer is the pillar of the religion. They turned to worldly desires, and will meet {trap}loss{/trap}.
now: Asr slides to just before Maghrib. Then it slides to tomorrow. {trap}It rarely starts with quitting; it starts with later.{/trap} The phone, the meeting, the show, one more round.
old: As long as I pray eventually, the timing does not matter much.
new: The slide starts with pushing prayer late; keeping its time protects me.
try: Pray your next prayer within the first fifteen minutes of its time.

title: Except those who repent, believe, and do good.
subtitle: The door stays open, and nothing is lost
then: Right after the warning comes the exception: those who turn back. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah accepts their repentance and gives them a good end{/reward}. Repentance wipes out what came before; the Prophet ﷺ said the one who repents is like one with no sin.
now: You read the last verse and felt it was about you: the missed prayers, the months of drifting. {reward}This verse is also about you.{/reward} The door is open, and none of your good deeds are lost.
old: I have slipped too far for it to matter now.
new: Turning back wipes the slate, and Allah wrongs me in nothing.
try: Make sincere tawbah today in your own words, then pray the next prayer on time.

title: Gardens promised in the unseen, and the promise will come.
subtitle: Believing in a home you have not seen
then: Ibn Kathir says these are eternal gardens that believers trust in {idea}though they have never seen them{/idea}, from strength of faith. {reward}Allah does not break His promise or change it.{/reward} Some explained: the promise comes to them, and they come to it.
now: You save for a house you will not see for years, trusting the plan. The pension letter promises something decades away. {reward}Allah's promise is more certain than any of them.{/reward}
old: What I cannot see is less real than what is in front of me.
new: Allah's promise of the unseen is the surest thing I have.
try: Spend two minutes today imagining the home Allah promised, and thank Him for it.

title: No empty talk there, only peace, and provision morning and evening.
subtitle: A place without useless or hurtful words
then: Ibn Kathir says Paradise has {trap}no ignorant, wasteful or useless speech{/trap} like this life, only peace. The Prophet ﷺ described its people as having no disputes or hatred, {reward}their hearts united like one heart{/reward}, glorifying Allah morning and evening.
now: Comment sections, office politics, the cousin who always picks a fight. {trap}So much noise you have stopped noticing it.{/trap} Picture a place where every word you hear is peace.
old: Arguments and gossip are just part of how people talk.
new: The speech of Paradise is peace, and I can practice it here.
try: Leave one group chat argument unanswered today, and say something kind instead.

title: That Paradise is inherited by the mindful servants.
subtitle: Who inherits it
then: Ibn Kathir describes the heirs as those {idea}who obey Allah in happiness and hardship, suppress their anger, and pardon people's offenses{/idea}. He links it to the start of Surah Al-Mu'minun: the believers who are humble in prayer are the inheritors of Firdaws.
now: Someone cuts you off in traffic. Someone at work takes credit for your idea. {idea}Holding your tongue and letting it go is what the heirs of Paradise do.{/idea}
old: Paradise is for people who never get angry.
new: Paradise is for those who feel anger and still hold it and forgive.
try: When anger rises today, stay quiet for ten seconds, then choose to pardon.

title: We descend only by your Lord's command, and He never forgets.
subtitle: Jibril's answer when visits paused
then: The Prophet ﷺ asked Jibril why he did not visit more often, and this verse came down. Ibn Abbas said a delay had {trap}disturbed and grieved{/trap} him. Mujahid explained the last words: {reward}your Lord has not forgotten you{/reward}.
now: You prayed for weeks and felt nothing. No answer, no sign, a long dry stretch. {reward}Your Lord is never forgetful.{/reward} Even the Prophet ﷺ felt a wait, and this was the reply.
old: When I feel nothing for a long time, Allah has forgotten me.
new: Help arrives on Allah's timing, and He never forgets me.
try: When you feel spiritually dry today, say: my Lord is never forgetful.

title: Worship Him and be patient in it; nothing is like Him.
subtitle: Patience is part of worship

picture.label: Who He is, what to do

row.title: Ar-Rahman
sub: a name no one else has

then: He created everything and controls it with no one to oppose Him. So worship Him and {reward}stay patient in it{/reward}. Ibn Abbas explained the question as: do you know anything comparable to the Lord? He also said {idea}no one else is named Ar-Rahman{/idea}.
now: Fajr in winter. Fasting in a long summer. Staying kind with a difficult parent. {reward}Worship is not only the act; it is the patience to keep at it day after day.{/reward}
old: If worship feels hard to keep up, I must be doing it wrong.
new: Worship takes patience, and that patience is itself worship.
try: Pick one act of worship you find hard and do it today with patience, not perfection.

title: Once I die, will I really be brought back alive?
subtitle: The human doubt about resurrection

key.label: How it feels vs what is true

then: Ibn Kathir says people are {trap}amazed that they could be returned to life after death{/trap} and think it far-fetched. The Quran records this doubt in several places, like: when we are dust, will we be a new creation?
now: Standing at a grave, watching the earth fill in, a quiet thought: is this really the end? {idea}The Quran does not hide that question; it answers it in the next verse.{/idea}
old: Life after death is hard to believe, so I avoid thinking about it.
new: I can face the question honestly, because Allah answers it.
try: Next time you pass a graveyard, pause and make dua for those buried there.

title: Does man not remember he was once nothing?
subtitle: The first creation proves the second

row.title: neither
sub: He began it, He repeats it

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}uses the beginning of creation as proof for its repetition{/idea}. He made man from nothing, so He can surely make him again. In a hadith qudsi, Allah says the second creation is not harder for Him than the first.
now: Scroll back to your baby photos. Before those, there was no you at all. {idea}The One who did that the first time has no trouble doing it again.{/idea}
old: Coming back to life sounds impossible.
new: My own existence from nothing is proof I will be brought back.
try: Look at your hand today and say: He made this from nothing, and He will remake it.

title: Allah swears He will gather them, with the devils too.
subtitle: A gathering no one can skip
then: Allah swears by His own Self that He will {trap}gather those who worshipped others, and their devils with them{/trap}. Ibn Abbas said they will be brought kneeling, and some said standing, around Hell.
now: The voices you follow now, the influences you let shape you, the whispers you obey. {idea}On that Day people stand with what they followed.{/idea} Today you still choose your company.
old: Who I follow and listen to is just a private preference.
new: I will stand with what I followed, so I choose it carefully now.
try: Unfollow one account or voice today that pulls you away from Allah.

title: From every group, the most defiant are taken first.
subtitle: Those who led others astray carry the most
then: Ibn Mas'ud said they will be gathered together, then {trap}Allah will begin with the greatest of them in crime{/trap}, one after another. The followers will blame the leaders who misled them, as described in Surah Al-A'raf.
now: You are the one others copy: the older sibling, the team lead, the friend who sets the tone. {idea}Your influence counts.{/idea} Use it to pull people toward good, not away from it.
old: What I encourage in others is their responsibility, not mine.
new: Leading others carries weight; I want my influence to lead toward Allah.
try: Use your influence today to encourage one person toward something good.

title: Allah knows best who most deserves the Fire.
subtitle: Judgment belongs to the One who knows all
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}Allah best knows which of His creatures deserve the Fire{/idea} and whose punishment is doubled. That knowledge belongs to Him, not to people.
now: It is easy to scroll and decide who is going where. {idea}That is Allah's knowledge, not yours.{/idea} The only person whose case you can work on is your own.
old: I can tell who is lost and who is saved.
new: Only Allah knows each person's end; my work is my own heart.
try: Catch yourself judging someone's fate today, and make dua for them instead.

title: Every one of you will pass over it.
subtitle: The bridge everyone must cross
then: Ibn Mas'ud described a bridge over Hell, sharp like a sword's edge. {idea}Some cross like lightning, some like wind, some like fast horses{/idea}, while angels pray: O Allah, save them. Ibn Kathir says each person's speed depends on their deeds in this life. It is a decree that will happen.
now: Every prayer you guard, every kindness you do quietly, every hurt you forgive. {idea}You are building your pace for a crossing everyone makes.{/idea} Nothing small is wasted.
old: The Day of Judgment is far away and unrelated to my ordinary day.
new: Today's ordinary deeds are shaping how I will cross.
try: Add one small good deed today with the crossing in mind.

title: Then Allah saves those who were mindful of Him.
subtitle: Rescue after the crossing
then: When the Prophet ﷺ said the people of Badr would not enter the Fire, Hafsah asked about the last verse. He recited this one: {reward}then We shall save those who had taqwa{/reward}. Ibn Kathir describes intercession, and believers brought out down to {reward}an atom's weight of faith{/reward}.
now: You feel your faith is small and patchy. Some days just a whispered la ilaha illallah. {reward}Allah's mercy reaches even the smallest faith.{/reward} Guard it, and grow it.
old: My faith is too small to count for anything.
new: Every grain of faith matters to Allah, so I protect and grow mine.
try: Say la ilaha illallah slowly ten times today, meaning every word.

title: Which side has the nicer houses and busier gatherings?
subtitle: Measuring truth by success
then: When the verses were recited, the disbelievers boasted to the believers: which group has {trap}the best homes and the busiest gatherings{/trap}? Ibn Kathir says they meant: how can we be wrong while living this well? The believers then were hiding in the house of Al-Arqam.
now: Their channel has a million followers. Their lifestyle looks perfect. {trap}It is easy to assume that whoever looks most successful must be right.{/trap} You check yourself: are you measuring truth by numbers?
old: If people are doing that well, they must be right.
new: Comfort and popularity do not prove anyone is right.
try: Notice one time today you judge something true just because it is popular.

title: Many richer, better-looking generations before them were destroyed.
subtitle: Wealth did not save those before
then: Allah answered their boast: how many generations before them were {trap}better in wealth, goods and appearance{/trap}, and were destroyed for denial? Ibn Abbas linked this to Fir'awn's people, who left behind gardens, springs and honored places.
now: The new car, the extension on the house, the perfect skin routine. {trap}None of it changes where you stand with Allah.{/trap} Look at what you are doing with it, not just how much there is.
old: Having more makes me safer.
new: What I have cannot protect me; only how I live can.
try: Use one thing you own today to help someone else.

title: Whoever is astray is given time, until they see the truth.
subtitle: Respite is not approval
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say: whoever is in error, {idea}whether from us or from you{/idea}, the Most Merciful extends their time. Then, when the promise comes, they will know who is truly worse in position. Ibn Kathir calls it a reply to their boast about houses and gatherings.
now: Nothing bad has happened, so the habit continues. Another month, another year. {idea}A long rope is mercy, and a chance to look again at where you are going.{/idea}
old: If nothing has gone wrong yet, I must be on the right track.
new: Time given is a chance to check my path, not proof that it is right.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: if the Hour came now, would I want to change anything?

title: Allah adds guidance to the guided; lasting good deeds are best.
subtitle: Guidance grows, and good deeds remain
then: After the misguided are given time that increases their misguidance, Allah says {idea}He increases the guided in guidance{/idea}. And {reward}the good deeds that last are better with your Lord{/reward}, in reward and in final outcome, unlike the houses and gatherings they boasted of.
now: You started with one prayer a day on time. Then two. Now you notice you want more. {idea}That is guidance growing.{/idea} Each step makes the next one easier.
old: I am not religious enough to make progress.
new: Every step toward Allah, He answers with more guidance.
try: Take one small step beyond your usual worship today.

title: He refused a worker's wage and mocked the Hereafter.
subtitle: Al-As bin Wa'il and the blacksmith Khabbab
then: Khabbab, a blacksmith in Makkah, made a sword for Al-As bin Wa'il. When he asked for his wage, {trap}Al-As refused unless Khabbab disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ{/trap}. Khabbab refused. Al-As mocked: when I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children and pay you then.
now: The client who keeps delaying the invoice. The boss who says: you will get paid when things pick up. {trap}Holding back someone's due is its own wrong.{/trap} Check whether you owe anyone right now.
old: Delaying what I owe someone is not a big deal.
new: Withholding someone's due is serious, and no one is guaranteed anything later.
try: Pay one debt or keep one financial promise today, however small.

title: Has he seen the unseen, or holds he a promise?
subtitle: The question that exposes false confidence

picture.label: Where would his certainty come from

row.title: I am sure I am fine

then: Allah challenges Al-As's boast: {idea}does he know the unseen{/idea}, so well he can swear to what he will have in the Hereafter? Or {idea}has he taken an agreement from the Most Merciful{/idea}? Neither.
now: I am a good person, I will be fine. You hear it, you maybe say it. {trap}It sounds humble, but it is a claim about the unseen.{/trap} Hope is good; certainty about yourself is not yours to claim.
old: I am sure I will be fine in the Hereafter.
new: I hope for Allah's mercy, but I hold no guarantee except what He promised.
try: Replace one I will be fine with: I hope for Allah's mercy, so let me act.

title: No: his words are recorded, and they count against him.
subtitle: Mocking words are written down
then: The word {idea}No{/idea} rejects his claim. Ibn Kathir says Allah will {trap}record what he says{/trap}: what he hopes for himself and his disbelief, and it will add to his punishment in the Hereafter.
now: The sarcastic comment, the joke at religion's expense, the post you laughed at and shared. {idea}Words feel light; they are written.{/idea} Think before you type.
old: What I say casually does not really matter.
new: Every word is recorded, so I choose mine with care.
try: Before sending any message today, ask: would I want this on my record?

title: We inherit what he boasts of, and he comes alone.
subtitle: No wealth, no children, just him
then: He claimed he would have more wealth and children in the Hereafter. Ibn Kathir says the opposite: {trap}Allah will take all of it from him{/trap}, and {idea}he will come to Allah alone{/idea}, without wealth or children.
now: The family photo on your lock screen. The savings app. {idea}On that Day you stand alone, carrying only what you did.{/idea} Love them, provide for them, and build your own record too.
old: My family and wealth will stand with me.
new: I will stand before Allah alone, so I prepare my own deeds.
try: Do one deed today purely for your own record with Allah.

title: They took other gods hoping to gain honor and power.
subtitle: Looking for strength in the wrong place
then: Ibn Kathir says they took gods besides Allah {trap}so these could be a source of honor and might for them{/trap}. They thought these gods would make them powerful and victorious.
now: The right contacts, the title, the brand you wear, the person you keep close for their influence. {trap}Things you lean on for status.{/trap} Ask what you are really relying on to feel strong.
old: My strength comes from my connections and status.
new: Real honor comes only from Allah.
try: Name one thing you lean on for status, and remind yourself who truly gives honor.

title: Those gods will deny them and turn against them.
subtitle: What you relied on becomes your opponent
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Judgment the things they worshipped will {trap}deny their worship and become their enemies{/trap}, the opposite of what they hoped. Ad-Dahhak said it means enemies; As-Suddi said severe opposition.
now: The friend you broke rules for, who drops you the moment it costs them. The job you gave everything to, that lets you go in an email. {trap}What you put before Allah eventually turns its back on you.{/trap}
old: What I give myself to will always be there for me.
new: Only Allah never turns away; everything else can fail me.
try: Reflect on one thing you put before Allah, and give that time to Him today.

title: The devils keep pushing those who turned away.
subtitle: Constant nudges toward wrong
then: Ibn Abbas said the devils {trap}lead them astray with temptation{/trap}. Qatadah said they harass them until they disobey Allah. Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd linked it to the verse: whoever turns from the remembrance of the Most Merciful is given a devil as companion.
now: The days you skip dhikr and Quran, the pull toward wrong feels stronger. One bad scroll leads to another. {idea}Remembrance is your guard; when it drops, the pushing starts.{/idea}
old: Temptation hits me randomly; there is nothing I can do.
new: Staying with Allah's remembrance protects me from constant pushes to wrong.
try: Say your morning or evening adhkar today, even just a few lines.

title: Do not be impatient; their days are being counted.
subtitle: Every hour of respite is numbered

key.label: Why wrong seems to go on

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ, while the believers were being persecuted: {idea}do not be hasty about them{/idea}. Their time is counted. As-Suddi said that means {idea}years, months, days and hours{/idea}. Ibn Kathir cites: do not think Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.
now: Someone wronged you and is still thriving, still smiling in the photos. {idea}Your impatience is understandable.{/idea} Allah is counting every hour; you can let go of the need to see it settled today.
old: If I do not see justice now, it will never come.
new: Allah counts every moment; justice is on His timing, not mine.
try: Hand one grievance over to Allah in dua today and stop replaying it.

title: The mindful arrive before the Most Merciful as honored guests.
subtitle: Gathered like a delegation
then: Ibn Kathir says the righteous will come {reward}like a delegation arriving before the Best Receiver of delegations{/reward}. Ibn Marzuq described the believer meeting a beautiful, fragrant figure: I am your righteous deeds. You carried me through life; now ride on me.
now: You carry your deeds every day: the early alarm, the patience with the kids, the charity no one sees. {reward}They feel heavy now. One day they carry you.{/reward}
old: Doing good is a burden I carry.
new: The good I carry now will carry me on the Day.
try: Do one good deed today and picture it waiting for you.

title: The criminals are driven, thirsty, toward Hell.
subtitle: The other arrival
then: Those who denied the Messengers will be driven to the Fire {trap}parched and thirsty{/trap}, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said. Ibn Kathir notes that here the earlier boast is answered: {idea}which of the two groups is better in position?{/idea}
now: Two people leave the same office party, one to a shift at the food bank, one to something they will regret. {idea}Every evening you choose which way you are walking.{/idea} The final arrival is shaped by all of them.
old: Where I end up is decided far away from today's choices.
new: Each day's choices decide whether I arrive honored or driven.
try: Make one choice tonight that you would want to be driven by on that Day.

title: Only those with a covenant from the Most Merciful can intercede.
subtitle: The covenant is la ilaha illallah
then: Ibn Abbas said the covenant is {idea}the testimony that none deserves worship but Allah{/idea}, accepting that all power is Allah's, and placing hope in Him alone. Those who deny will say: we have no intercessors and no close friend.
now: Your phone has every contact you might need: the lawyer, the doctor, the cousin with connections. {idea}On that Day, the only connection that counts is la ilaha illallah, lived out.{/idea}
old: Knowing the right people will get me through.
new: My real covenant is la ilaha illallah and hope in Allah alone.
try: Renew the testimony today slowly, and ask what it asks of you this week.

title: They say the Most Merciful has taken a son.
subtitle: After Isa's story, the claim is addressed
then: Ibn Kathir says that after the surah showed Isa as a {idea}servant of Allah{/idea} born to Maryam without a father, it {trap}refutes the claim that Allah has a son{/trap}. Holy and exalted is He above that.
now: You might never say this claim, but you can still slip into picturing Allah too small, like a human with needs. {idea}This passage is about getting Allah's greatness right in your own heart.{/idea}
old: How I picture Allah is a minor detail.
new: Knowing Allah as One, needing nothing, is the center of my faith.
try: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas three times today, slowly, thinking about each line.

title: You have said a monstrous thing.
subtitle: Some words are heavier than any deed
then: Allah addresses the claim directly: you have brought something {trap}terrible{/trap}. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Malik all explained the word idda as terrible.
now: A joke about Allah in the group chat. A careless line about religion on a podcast. {trap}Words about Allah are never small.{/trap} Notice how you speak about Him, even in jest.
old: Talking loosely about Allah is harmless.
new: Words about Allah carry great weight, so I speak of Him with respect.
try: Correct yourself kindly the next time you speak of Allah carelessly.

title: The heavens almost tear, the earth splits, mountains collapse.
subtitle: Creation's reaction to the claim
then: Ibn Kathir says creation reacts this way {idea}out of high esteem for Allah{/idea}, because all creatures stand upon His Oneness. Ibn Abbas said everything except humans and jinn is frightened by associating partners with Allah.
now: You stand on a mountain, under a night sky, and feel small. {idea}Everything around you is quietly glorifying Allah.{/idea} Your heart can join them, or stay numb.
old: The world around me is just matter, with no feelings toward Allah.
new: All of creation honors Allah's Oneness, and I can stand with it.
try: Step outside tonight, look up, and say subhanallah.

title: All this because they claim the Most Merciful has a son.
subtitle: And still He provides for them
then: The cause of creation's distress is named: {trap}they ascribe a son to the Most Merciful{/trap}. Yet the Prophet ﷺ said {reward}no one is more patient than Allah with hurtful words{/reward}; they ascribe a son to Him, and He gives them health and sustenance.
now: Someone insults you, and you cut them off within the hour. {reward}Allah hears the worst said about Him and keeps feeding the one who said it.{/reward} Think about your own patience with people.
old: When someone wrongs me, I should cut them off immediately.
new: Allah's patience with people can teach me patience with them too.
try: Show patience to one person today who tests you.

title: It does not befit the Most Merciful to take a son.
subtitle: Beyond any equal or need
then: Ibn Kathir says a son is {idea}not befitting His lofty majesty and greatness{/idea}. He has no equal in His creation, because all creatures are His servants. He is the One, the Self-Sufficient, whom everything needs.
now: You lean on so many things: coffee, savings, the right people. Everything needs something. {idea}Allah alone needs nothing at all.{/idea} That is why you can lean on Him completely.
old: Allah is great, but somehow like the things I know.
new: Allah is beyond any need or likeness, so I can rely on Him fully.
try: In one worry today, say: Allah needs nothing, and I need Him.

title: Everyone in the heavens and earth comes to Him as a servant.
subtitle: No exceptions in all creation
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}all creatures are His slaves{/idea}, so none could be His child or equal. Earlier in the surah, Isa's first words were exactly this: I am the servant of Allah.
now: The CEO and the cleaner in the same lift. The celebrity and the nurse in the same prayer row. {idea}Before Allah, every one of them is a servant.{/idea} So are you, no higher and no lower.
old: Some people are above the rest of us.
new: Everyone, without exception, is a servant of the Most Merciful.
try: Treat one person today you might overlook with the same respect as anyone important.

title: He has counted every one of them exactly.
subtitle: No one is lost in the crowd
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}knows their number from creation until the Day of Resurrection{/idea}, male and female, young and old. Not one is missed.
now: Eight billion people. You are one face on a crowded train, one number on a waiting list. {reward}Allah has counted you, individually, exactly.{/reward}
old: I am too small for anyone to notice.
new: Allah knows me individually; I am never lost to Him.
try: Say to Allah today: You know me. Then tell Him one thing on your heart.

title: Each of them comes to Him alone on the Day.
subtitle: No helper but Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}there will be no helper and no one to save him except Allah alone{/idea}. He judges as He wills and {reward}does not do even an atom's weight of injustice{/reward}.
now: You hate being alone at the doctor's or in a new city. {idea}That Day you stand alone, but before the Most Just, who wrongs no one.{/idea} Build your relationship with Him now.
old: Being alone before Allah is something to fear and avoid thinking about.
new: I will stand alone before a just and merciful Lord, so I get close to Him now.
try: Spend five minutes alone with Allah today, just you and Him.

title: For those who believe and do good, Allah plants love.
subtitle: Love placed in hearts by the Most Merciful
then: The Prophet ﷺ said when Allah loves a servant, {reward}He tells Jibril to love him{/reward}; Jibril calls to the heavens, and acceptance is placed for him on earth. Abu Hurayrah said this is the meaning of this verse. Ibn Kathir calls it certain.
now: You work so hard to be liked: the right replies, the perfect photos, saying yes to everything. {reward}The love that truly settles in hearts is the one Allah places.{/reward}
old: I need to work hard to make people like me.
new: When I seek Allah's love through faith and good deeds, He places love for me in hearts.
try: Do one good deed today purely for Allah, not to be liked.

title: Made easy in your tongue, to give good news and warn.
subtitle: The Quran's two jobs
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ the Quran was made easy {idea}in pure, eloquent Arabic{/idea}. Its purpose: {reward}good news for those who respond{/reward}, and a warning for those who turn from the truth toward falsehood.
now: You opened this app, read a verse, and something in you moved. {idea}That is the Quran doing what it was made easy to do.{/idea} The good news is for you; so is the warning.
old: The Quran is too difficult for someone like me.
new: Allah made the Quran easy so it could reach me.
try: Read the meaning of one short verse today and share its good news with someone.

title: Can you hear even a whisper of them now?
subtitle: The surah ends in silence
then: Allah asks about the nations who rejected His signs: {trap}can you see a single one of them, or hear even a whisper?{/trap} Ibn Abbas and others said it means any sound at all. The surah that opened with Zakariyya's quiet prayer closes in silence.
now: The trending names of ten years ago. The loud figures everyone talked about. {trap}Most of them are already silent.{/trap} {reward}What will still speak for you is what you did for Allah.{/reward}
old: Being loud and known now means I will be remembered.
new: Noise fades; only deeds done for Allah stay.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that will outlast any post you make.
